The tumor was found in both left and right sides, mostly in the mid and peripheral zones with a Gleason score of 3+4=7/10. The tumor does not have extraprostatic extension, and there is no tumor seen in the seminal vesicles or at the specimen margins. The TNM stage is pT2c, pNX, pMX, which indicates that the tumor is organ-confined, but the lymph nodes and distant metastasis are unknown.

According to the AJCC Cancer Staging Manual (7th edition), the T stage for prostate adenocarcinoma is determined by the extent of the tumor. T1 stage indicates that the tumor is not palpable or visible by imaging. T2 stage indicates that the tumor is organ-confined, and T3 stage indicates that the tumor has extraprostatic extension. T4 stage indicates that the tumor invades adjacent structures.

In this case, the patient's tumor is organ-confined, and there is no extraprostatic extension or invasion of adjacent structures. Therefore, the T stage is T2. The T2 stage is further divided into T2a, T2b, and T2c, depending on the extent of the tumor. T2a indicates that the tumor involves one half of one lobe or less, T2b indicates that the tumor involves more than one half of one lobe but not both lobes, and T2c indicates that the tumor involves both lobes. The pathology report indicates that the tumor involves both lobes, so the T stage is T2c.
